direct_exposure.basis: One ACTIVE, role-evidenced placement: Caterpillar's ACERT architecture (NOx reduction system, DOC, DPF) is the integrated Tier 4 Final aftertreatment package on its large reciprocating-engine gensets, exactly the emission-control content a minor-NSR permit application must characterize. No disclosed revenue percentage attributes any dollar figure to the aftertreatment package specifically; Caterpillar is a $67.6bn diversified equipment and engine maker (FY2025 revenue, SEC companyfacts) and this is one component of one product line within it. A second ACTIVE placement on the same chain, onsite-reciprocating-gensets (link_heat CROWDED, not money_corner), is the genset-restart story rather than the catalyst story and is not part of this promotion.

capture.basis: The chain scores emissions-aftertreatment-and-catalyst capture at 65, the strongest capture case on this map: a permit written to an SCR-based BACT presumption leaves an engine no other way to meet it (low component-level substitutability), and the disclosed comparable is Johnson Matthey's $360m acquisition of Cormetech, guided to more than GBP200m in sales at mid-teens operating margins by 2026/27 (company's own guidance, not a market-size inference). Caterpillar's own FY2025 operating margin is 16.5% company-wide, consistent with but not proof of a mid-teens-or-better margin on the aftertreatment line specifically. Held below full lock-in because substitutability at the PATH level is high: a developer that switches to fuel cells at chain position 7 removes the aftertreatment content entirely.

heat.basis: Ember scores this link UNDISCOVERED with crowdedness 28, the thinnest attention on the chain: the only listed pure play whose business is the catalyst itself, Johnson Matthey, sits at the bottom of its own 52-week range three months after buying the segment's named global leader (Cormetech) rather than that leader ever being listed. Caterpillar and Cummins are diversified engine OEMs whose stock prices trade on the genset and equipment story, not this specific catalyst content, which is exactly what leaves the aftertreatment exposure genuinely undiscovered rather than merely under-covered.

quality.basis: All 12 canonical fields carry a sourced number as of the 2026-09-06 re-fetch under the corrected concept map (commit series fixing FUEL-TECH/CATERPILLAR/CUMMINS/ONT concept coverage); zero NULL. Piotroski 5 of 9 is middling rather than strong, Beneish -2.405 is CLEAN, net_debt_to_ebitda 1.79x is moderate leverage for a heavy-equipment maker, and operating cash flow exceeds net income (1.32x).
quality.counterweight: Quality describes Caterpillar's whole balance sheet and earnings discipline, not the size or durability of the aftertreatment product line specifically; a middling F-score is a real caution on the parent, not a comment on this one link.

expectations_gap.basis: The reverse DCF solves a 28.57% five-year implied FCF CAGR against an achieved three-year revenue CAGR of 4.38%. The roughly 24-point gap exceeds the 12.34-point horizon_spread, so this reads as a real gap rather than a horizon-convention artifact: the market is pricing meaningfully faster cash-flow growth than Caterpillar's recent top-line has delivered. Whether the AI/data-center-driven genset and aftertreatment cycle can plausibly close a gap this size is Stocky's question, not this profile's; recorded plainly here.
